extra_vocab.en: full of energy and new ideas
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於徵才廣告、公司介紹和市場報告，形容人或團隊積極有衝勁，也可形容市場或情況一直在變化。語氣正面。

example.en: We are proud of our young and dynamic team.
example.zh: 我們以年輕又有活力的團隊為傲。

example.en: The mobile phone industry is a dynamic market with fast changes.
example.zh: 手機產業是一個變化快速的市場。

example.en: The board chose a dynamic leader to guide the company.
example.zh: 董事會選了一位有衝勁的領導者來帶領公司。

examples.en: We are looking for a dynamic person to join our sales team.
examples.zh: 我們正在找一位有活力的人加入銷售團隊。

examples.en: Our dynamic website updates prices in real time.
examples.zh: 我們的動態網站會即時更新價格。

examples.en: The company is known for its fast and dynamic culture.
examples.zh: 這家公司以快速、有活力的文化聞名。

confusable.diff: dynamics 是名詞，指團體內部互相影響的方式或變化的力量；dynamic 是形容詞。
confusable.usage: dynamics 是名詞，常見於 team dynamics（團隊互動）；dynamic 是形容詞，修飾名詞。

example.en: Good team dynamics help us finish projects on time.
example.zh: 良好的團隊互動幫助我們準時完成專案。

similar.diff: energetic 強調體力和精神充沛；dynamic 還包含有想法、有衝勁。

example.en: The energetic trainer kept everyone excited all day.
example.zh: 這位精力充沛的訓練師讓大家整天都很興奮。

similar.diff: active 是積極參與、常有行動；dynamic 語氣更強，帶有變化與創意。

example.en: She is an active member of our sales club.
example.zh: 她是我們銷售社團的積極成員。

example.en: He plays an active role in every meeting.
example.zh: 他在每場會議中都扮演積極的角色。

example.en: The new manager is young and energetic.
example.zh: 新經理年輕又精力充沛。

example.en: We offer flexible working hours to all staff.
example.zh: 我們提供所有員工彈性的上班時間。

example.en: Our office has a modern design.
example.zh: 我們的辦公室有現代的設計。

senses.en: full of energy and new ideas

example.en: She is a dynamic speaker who keeps the audience interested.
example.zh: 她是個有活力的講者，讓聽眾一直保持興趣。

senses.distinguish: 旁邊出現 market、system、pricing 等字時，通常指不斷變化的。

example.en: The system uses dynamic pricing based on how many seats are left.
example.zh: 這個系統根據剩餘座位數使用動態定價。

extra_vocab.zh: 乏味的、不鋒利的、暗淡的
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於形容簡報、工作乏味，也可形容刀具不利、顏色暗淡或市場不景氣。要依上下文判斷是哪一種意思。

example.en: The new design looks duller than the old one.
example.zh: 新設計看起來比舊的更暗淡乏味。

example.en: That was the dullest presentation I have seen this year.
example.zh: 那是我今年看過最無聊的簡報。

example.en: Heavy use dulls the blade of this machine within a month.
example.zh: 大量使用會讓這台機器的刀片在一個月內變鈍。

example.en: Long hours of repeated work dulled the staff's interest.
example.zh: 長時間的重複工作使員工的興趣減退了。

example.en: Cold weather is dulling the shine of the new paint.
example.zh: 寒冷的天氣正在讓新油漆的光澤變暗。

example.en: Dull colors on the poster will not attract young customers.
example.zh: 海報上暗淡的顏色無法吸引年輕顧客。

example.en: He felt a dull pain in his back after the flight.
example.zh: 搭完飛機後，他的背隱隱作痛。

example.en: Sales stayed low because of the dull market this winter.
example.zh: 因為今年冬天市場不景氣，銷售一直偏低。

examples.en: The training session was long and dull for most staff.
examples.zh: 這場培訓對大多數員工來說又長又無聊。

examples.en: The packaging looks dull, so we should try something brighter.
examples.zh: 這個包裝看起來很暗淡，我們應該試試更鮮明的。

examples.en: A dull grey sky covered the city all week.
examples.zh: 灰暗的天空整個星期都籠罩著這座城市。

confusable.diff: dual 是「雙重的、兩個的」，發音 /ˈduːəl/；dull 是「乏味的、鈍的」。

example.en: This room has a dual purpose as an office and a studio.
example.zh: 這個房間兼具辦公室和工作室的雙重用途。

similar.diff: boring 只指「無聊的」，最常見；dull 還可以指不鋒利、不鮮明。

example.en: The meeting was so boring that I almost fell asleep.
example.zh: 這場會議太無聊了，我差點睡著。

example.en: Some people find data entry boring.
example.zh: 有些人覺得資料輸入很無聊。

example.en: The room is bright and has a nice view.
example.zh: 這個房間很明亮，景色也很好。

example.en: Be careful with the sharp knife in the kitchen.
example.zh: 請小心廚房裡的鋒利刀子。

example.en: Business is usually quiet in January.
example.zh: 一月的生意通常比較清淡。

pos_uses.zh: 乏味的、不鋒利的、暗淡的

example.en: Many people find routine office work dull after a few years.
example.zh: 許多人做了幾年例行的辦公室工作後會覺得乏味。

example.en: Pain medicine can dull the pain for a few hours.
example.zh: 止痛藥可以讓疼痛減輕幾個小時。

example.en: The report was dull, so many people stopped reading it.
example.zh: 這份報告很乏味，所以很多人讀到一半就不看了。

senses.distinguish: 形容 knife、blade、scissors 等工具時，指不鋒利。

example.en: A dull knife makes cutting meat slow and unsafe.
example.zh: 鈍刀讓切肉又慢又不安全。

senses.distinguish: 形容 color、light、sound 時，指不鮮明、不清楚。

example.en: The dull light in the hall made reading difficult.
example.zh: 大廳裡昏暗的燈光讓閱讀變得困難。

extra_vocab.en: in or toward the main business area of a city
extra_vocab.note: 美式英語常見的字，多益用於辦公室位置、交通和約會情境，例如 downtown office、go downtown。英式英語多說 city centre。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: downtown 當副詞時前面不加 to 或 in，直接說 go downtown；當形容詞時放在名詞前，如 downtown office。

example.en: Rents in the downtown area are rising every year.
example.zh: 市中心地區的租金逐年上漲。

example.en: Our downtown office will move to a larger building next spring.
example.zh: 我們市中心的辦公室明年春天會搬到更大的大樓。

example.en: We will head downtown right after the meeting ends.
example.zh: 會議一結束，我們就前往市中心。

examples.en: Is there a good restaurant near your downtown hotel?
examples.zh: 你市中心的飯店附近有好餐廳嗎？

examples.en: I need to go downtown to meet a client at noon.
examples.zh: 我中午要到市中心去見一位客戶。

examples.en: Traffic downtown is heavy during the lunch hour.
examples.zh: 午餐時間市中心的交通很壅塞。

confusable.diff: uptown 指離市中心較遠的住宅區或城市北邊；downtown 是商業中心區。

example.en: Many families live uptown, away from the busy city center.
example.zh: 許多家庭住在遠離繁忙市中心的住宅區。

similar.diff: city center 意思相近，美英都可用，也可說 town center；downtown 是美式口語。

example.en: The hotel is in the city center, near the main station.
example.zh: 這間飯店位於市中心，靠近主要車站。

example.en: Traffic was heavy because of the rain.
example.zh: 因為下雨，車流很多。

example.en: Parking is free for all hotel guests.
example.zh: 飯店住客都可免費停車。

example.en: The subway is the fastest way to the airport.
example.zh: 地鐵是去機場最快的方式。

example.en: The shop is in a quiet neighborhood.
example.zh: 這家店在安靜的社區裡。

example.en: The downtown branch of our bank opens at nine.
example.zh: 我們銀行的市中心分行九點開門。

example.en: She works downtown, so she takes the subway every day.
example.zh: 她在市中心上班，所以每天搭地鐵。

example.en: The mayor has a plan to improve the downtown.
example.zh: 市長有一個改善市中心的計畫。

extra_vocab.en: the amount of medicine you take at one time
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於藥品標示、醫療和疫苗情境，指一次要吃或注射的量。也可用來比喻「一點點」某種事物。

example.en: The label says to take two doses a day.
example.zh: 標籤上寫著一天服用兩次劑量。

example.en: The nurse dosed each patient at the correct time.
example.zh: 護理師在正確的時間給每位病人服藥。

example.en: The clinic is dosing patients under a doctor's guidance.
example.zh: 診所正在醫生的指導下替病人給藥。

example.en: Do not take more than the recommended dose.
example.zh: 請勿超過建議的劑量服用。

example.en: The daily dose is printed on the side of the box.
example.zh: 每日劑量印在盒子的側面。

example.en: He took a dose of cold medicine before the meeting.
example.zh: 他在會議前吃了一劑感冒藥。

examples.en: The label shows the correct dose for adults.
examples.zh: 標籤上標明了成人的正確劑量。

examples.en: Take one dose after each meal, as the nurse explained.
examples.zh: 照護理師說明的，每餐後服用一次劑量。

examples.en: The second dose of the vaccine is next month.
examples.zh: 疫苗的第二劑在下個月。

confusable.diff: does 是 do 的第三人稱單數，發音 /dʌz/；dose 發音 /doʊs/，兩字拼法相近。
confusable.usage: does 是動詞（助動詞），dose 是名詞或動詞；兩者發音不同。

example.en: The doctor does not allow a double dose.
example.zh: 醫生不允許服用兩倍劑量。

similar.diff: amount 是一般的「數量」；dose 專指藥或輻射一次的規定份量。

example.en: The amount of medicine in each bottle is the same.
example.zh: 每瓶藥的份量都相同。

example.en: Keep the medicine away from children.
example.zh: 請把藥放在孩子拿不到的地方。

example.en: Take one tablet with water.
example.zh: 請配水服用一顆藥片。

example.en: You need a prescription to buy this drug.
example.zh: 你需要處方才能買這種藥。

example.en: The pharmacy is open until ten at night.
example.zh: 藥局開到晚上十點。

derived.link: dose + -age，表示規定的劑量，像 package、storage

example.en: A small dose of this medicine is safe for children.
example.zh: 小劑量的這種藥對孩子是安全的。

example.en: The nurse will dose each patient twice a day.
example.zh: 護理師會每天兩次給每位病人服藥。

senses.en: the amount of medicine you take at one time

example.en: Check the dose carefully before you give it to a child.
example.zh: 給孩子服藥前，請仔細確認劑量。

senses.zh: 一點點（某種經驗或特質）
senses.en: a small amount of something, often something not pleasant
senses.distinguish: 前面常接 a dose of + 抽象名詞，如 a dose of reality，是比喻用法。

example.en: The new manager brought a dose of fresh energy to the team.
example.zh: 新經理為團隊帶來了一點新的活力。

extra_vocab.en: to give money or things to help others
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於公益活動、公司社會責任和募款情境，捐出金錢、物品、血液或時間。語氣正面。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: donate 後面用 to 帶出接受者：donate A to B；不能說 donate B A，和 give 不同。

example.en: The bank donates ten percent of its profit to charity every year.
example.zh: 這家銀行每年把百分之十的利潤捐給慈善機構。

example.en: Several firms donated food and water after the storm.
example.zh: 暴風雨後，好幾家公司捐贈了食物和水。

example.en: He is donating books to the new community library.
example.zh: 他正在把書捐給新的社區圖書館。

example.en: Many customers choose to donate money to the new library.
example.zh: 許多顧客選擇捐錢給新的圖書館。

example.en: Employees can donate blood at the clinic on Friday.
example.zh: 員工星期五可以在診所捐血。

example.en: We plan to donate our old computers to local schools.
example.zh: 我們打算把舊電腦捐給當地學校。

examples.en: The company plans to donate part of its profit this year.
examples.zh: 公司計畫今年捐出部分利潤。

examples.en: Staff can donate old clothes at the front desk.
examples.zh: 員工可以在櫃檯捐出舊衣服。

examples.en: She decided to donate her time as a hospital volunteer.
examples.zh: 她決定捐出時間，擔任醫院志工。

confusable.diff: dominate 是「支配、主導」，拼法和 donate 相近，但意思完全不同。

example.en: Two large firms dominate the local electronics market.
example.zh: 兩家大公司主導著當地的電子產品市場。

similar.diff: contribute 可以是捐錢，也可以是貢獻時間或意見；donate 主要指免費捐出錢或物品。

example.en: Each employee contributed ten dollars to the gift.
example.zh: 每位員工都出了十美元買禮物。

similar.diff: give 是最一般的「給」，可接雙受詞；donate 要用 to，語氣較正式。

example.en: Please give the old files to the new assistant.
example.zh: 請把舊檔案交給新來的助理。

example.en: The charity helps families in need.
example.zh: 這個慈善機構幫助有需要的家庭。

example.en: We started a fund for the school project.
example.zh: 我們為學校專案成立了一個基金。

example.en: Volunteers will hand out food at the event.
example.zh: 志工會在活動中發放食物。

example.en: Each guest received a small gift.
example.zh: 每位賓客都收到一份小禮物。

derived.link: donate 去 e 加 -ion，變成名詞，像 decorate → decoration
donate 去 -ate 加 -or，捐東西的人，像 actor、visitor

extra_vocab.en: money a company pays to people who own its shares
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於財報、投資和股東通知，指公司把部分利潤分給股東。常搭配動詞 pay、declare、receive。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: dividend 是可數名詞，常用複數 dividends；常搭配動詞 pay、declare、receive。

example.en: Some companies use profits to pay dividends instead of expanding.
example.zh: 有些公司把利潤用來發股息，而不是擴張。

example.en: The company will pay a dividend to all shareholders in June.
example.zh: 公司將在六月向所有股東發放股息。

example.en: The quarterly dividend will be paid on the first of March.
example.zh: 季度股息將在三月一日發放。

example.en: A dividend payment was sent to every shareholder today.
example.zh: 股息已在今天寄給每位股東。

examples.en: The board announced a higher dividend for this quarter.
examples.zh: 董事會宣布本季提高股息。

examples.en: Many investors choose this stock because of its steady dividend.
examples.zh: 許多投資人因為股息穩定而選擇這支股票。

examples.en: Shareholders will receive their dividend by the end of the month.
examples.zh: 股東會在月底前收到股息。

confusable.diff: interest 是銀行存款或貸款的利息；dividend 是公司給股東的利潤。

example.en: The bank pays interest on every savings account.
example.zh: 銀行對每個儲蓄帳戶支付利息。

similar.diff: bonus 是公司給員工的額外獎金；dividend 是公司給股東的利潤。

example.en: Every employee received a year-end bonus this December.
example.zh: 每位員工今年十二月都領到年終獎金。

example.en: Each shareholder received a copy of the annual report.
example.zh: 每位股東都收到一份年度報告。

example.en: The stock price rose after the announcement.
example.zh: 公告後，股價上漲了。

example.en: The firm made a large profit last year.
example.zh: 這家公司去年賺了很大的利潤。

example.en: Real estate can be a safe investment.
example.zh: 不動產可以是一種安全的投資。

derived.link: 最基礎的字；dividend 是把利潤分給股東的錢
divide 去 de 加 -sion，變成名詞，像 decide → decision

senses.en: money a company pays to people who own its shares

example.en: The company has paid a steady dividend for ten years.
example.zh: 這家公司十年來都穩定發放股息。

senses.en: a good result you get from earlier work
senses.distinguish: 常用 pay dividends，是比喻用法，意思是「帶來回報」。

example.en: Training new staff will pay dividends in the long run.
example.zh: 培訓新員工長遠來看會帶來回報。

extra_vocab.zh: 使人分心的事物；干擾選項
extra_vocab.en: something that takes your attention away from what you are doing
extra_vocab.note: 指讓人無法專心的人或事物。在測驗題中，也指看起來正確、其實不對的干擾選項。

example.en: Several distractors in the room made it hard to finish the test.
example.zh: 房間裡好幾項干擾讓人很難完成測驗。

example.en: Remove distractors from your desk before you start the report.
example.zh: 開始寫報告前，先把桌上讓你分心的東西移走。

example.en: The wrong answer serves as a distractor in the listening test.
example.zh: 錯誤的答案在聽力測驗中充當干擾選項。

example.en: Social media is a major distractor for many young workers.
example.zh: 社群媒體是許多年輕上班族的主要干擾。

examples.en: Turn off your phone, because notifications can be a big distractor.
examples.zh: 請關掉手機，因為通知可能是很大的干擾。

examples.en: In this multiple-choice test, answer C is a clever distractor.
examples.zh: 在這份選擇題測驗中，答案 C 是個巧妙的干擾選項。

examples.en: Music with words can become a distractor while you study.
examples.zh: 有歌詞的音樂在讀書時可能會使人分心。

confusable.diff: distraction 是「分心」這件事或讓人分心的東西；distractor 更常指刻意造成干擾的選項或事物。
confusable.usage: distraction 可指分心的狀態，也可數可不可數；distractor 是可數名詞，多指具體的干擾物或選項。

example.en: The noise outside was a constant distraction during the call.
example.zh: 通話期間，外面的噪音一直讓人分心。

similar.diff: interruption 是打斷正在做的事；distractor 是讓你注意力跑掉的東西。

example.en: Phone calls are a constant interruption during meetings.
example.zh: 電話一直在會議中造成打斷。

example.en: Please focus on the main goal of the project.
example.zh: 請專注於專案的主要目標。

example.en: Please pay attention to the safety rules.
example.zh: 請注意安全規定。

example.en: Street noise makes it hard to work here.
example.zh: 街上的噪音讓人很難在這裡工作。

example.en: I cannot concentrate with the radio on.
example.zh: 收音機開著，我沒辦法集中精神。

derived.link: 最基礎的字；distractor = distract + -or，造成分心的東西，像 actor、visitor

senses.en: something that takes your attention away

example.en: The loud street became a distractor during the online meeting.
example.zh: 在線上會議期間，吵鬧的街道造成了干擾。

senses.en: a wrong answer that looks like a right one
senses.distinguish: 出現在 test、question、answer 的上下文時，指干擾選項。

example.en: The test writer adds a distractor that sounds almost correct.
example.zh: 出題者加入一個聽起來幾乎正確的干擾選項。

extra_vocab.en: to send someone or something to a place
extra_vocab.note: 多益常見於物流、客服和公司通知，指派人或把貨物、文件送出。名詞也可指快訊、報導。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: dispatch 當動詞時常接 sb／sth + to + 地點；被動寫成 be dispatched to。

example.en: Daily dispatches from our reporter cover the trade talks.
example.zh: 我們記者每天的報導都涵蓋貿易會談。

example.en: The warehouse dispatches about two hundred packages every day.
example.zh: 倉庫每天發出大約兩百個包裹。

example.en: The goods were dispatched from our Taipei warehouse yesterday.
example.zh: 貨物昨天已從我們台北的倉庫發出。

example.en: The manager is dispatching extra drivers to the airport today.
example.zh: 經理今天正在派額外的司機到機場。

example.en: The company will dispatch a team to repair the power line.
example.zh: 公司會派一個小組去修理電線。

example.en: We cannot dispatch goods until the payment is confirmed.
example.zh: 在確認付款之前，我們無法發出貨物。

example.en: Call the dispatch center if the driver is late.
example.zh: 如果司機遲到，請打電話給調度中心。

examples.en: We will dispatch a technician to your office tomorrow morning.
examples.zh: 我們明天早上會派一位技術人員到你的辦公室。

examples.en: We usually dispatch your order within twenty-four hours.
examples.zh: 我們通常會在二十四小時內寄出你的訂單。

examples.en: The reporter sent a short dispatch from the conference in Berlin.
examples.zh: 記者從柏林的會議現場發回一則簡短的快訊。

confusable.diff: dispense 是「分發、配（藥）」，拼法和 dispatch 相近；dispatch 是「派遣、寄出」。

example.en: The machine will dispense a cold drink for one dollar.
example.zh: 這台機器一美元就會送出一杯冷飲。

similar.diff: send 是最一般的「寄、送」；dispatch 更正式，強調迅速派出。

example.en: Please send the signed form to our head office.
example.zh: 請把簽好的表格寄到我們總公司。

similar.diff: ship 專指把貨物運送出去；dispatch 還可以指派人。

example.en: We ship all orders by air within two days.
example.zh: 我們兩天內以空運運送所有訂單。

example.en: Delivery usually takes two to three days.
example.zh: 送貨通常需要兩到三天。

example.en: Your order will arrive by Friday.
example.zh: 你的訂單星期五前會送到。

example.en: The shipment left the port this morning.
example.zh: 這批貨今天早上離開了港口。

example.en: The driver will call you before arriving.
example.zh: 司機到達前會先打電話給你。

example.en: The firm will dispatch a driver as soon as you call.
example.zh: 你一打電話，公司就會派司機過去。

example.en: The dispatch of new staff to Asia begins in May.
example.zh: 派遣新員工到亞洲的工作五月開始。

senses.en: the act of sending someone or something

example.en: Same-day dispatch is available for orders placed before noon.
example.zh: 中午前下的訂單可以當天寄出。

senses.en: a short news report sent from a place
senses.distinguish: 出現 reporter、news、newspaper 時，指記者發回的報導。

example.en: The newspaper printed a dispatch from its Paris office.
example.zh: 報紙刊登了巴黎辦公室發回的一則快訊。
